sentences.text: Respondent No.2 who is served in the matter has remained unrepresented before this Court.

NC: 2024:KHC:37602 3. FIR in crime No.1/2024 was registered by R.T.Nagar Police Station, Bengaluru city, against the petitioner herein initially for the offences under Section 67(B) of the Information Technology Act 2008, Sections 366, 376 & 506 of IPC and Sections 5(L) & 6 of POCSO Act., on the basis of the first information dated 03.01.2024 received from respondent No.2 herein, who is the father of the victim girl, aged about 16 years.
During the course of investigation of the case, the petitioner herein was arrested and remanded to judicial custody on 04.01.2024.
Investigation in the case is now completed and charge sheet has been filed against the petitioner for the aforesaid offences.
4. Bail application filed by the petitioner before the Court of the Jurisdictional Sessions Court in Crl.Misc. No.24904/2024 was rejected on 25.04.2024.
Therefore, he is before this Court.

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioner and the victim girl are in love, her parents had NC: 2024:KHC:37602 opposed their relationship.
The victim girl has not made any serious allegation against the petitioner in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
She has stated before the Magistrate that after attaining the age of 18 years she will be marrying the petitioner.

He also submits that the allegation against the petitioner about forwarding obscene photographs and videographs of the victim girl to the first informant was found to be false, and therefore, Section 67(B) of the Information Technology Act, 2018 is now dropped in the charge sheet.
Petitioner has no criminal antecedents.
Accordingly, prays to allow the petition.
6. Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the bail petition, he submits that undisputedly, the victim girl is a minor and she had stated that the petitioner had sexual intercourse with the minor girl.
Therefore, charge sheeted offences get attracted against the petitioner.
Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the petition.
First informant had approached the Police on 03.01.2024 and submitted his first information alleging that the petitioner was pestering his minor daughter, who was aged about 16 years, to love him.
He also threatened that if she does not love him, he will through acid on her face.

Therefore,
the victim girl allegedly had agreed to love the petitioner.
On 24.10.2023 petitioner had taken the victim girl along with him to his house and had sexual intercourse with her against her wishes.
It is alleged that he also captured obscene photos and videographs of the victim girl in his mobile phone and thereafter threatened her.
It is further alleged that he had asked the first informant to perform his marriage with the victim girl and threatened him with dire consequences.
It is also alleged that the obscene photographs and videographs of the victim girl captured by the petitioner was subsequently forwarded to the first informant.
During the course of the investigation petitioner was arrested and remanded to the judicial custody on 04.01.2024.
Investigation in the case is now completed and charge sheet has been filed.
During the course of investigation mobile phone of the petitioner and the first informant was sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory for examination.
Forensic Science Laboratory has now issued the report, which would go to show that the petitioner had not forwarded any photographs and videographs to the mobile of the first informant as alleged.
It is under these circumstances while filing charge sheet offence punishable under Section 67(B) of the Information Technology Act, is dropped.

During the course of investigation the statement of the victim girl has recorded by the jurisdictional Magistrate and in the said statement the victim girl was stated she was in love with the petitioner and she had accompanied him voluntarily.
She also has stated that her father opposed her relationship.
She has further stated after she attains the age of 18 years she will be marrying the petitioner.
The medical record of the victim girl would go to show that there was no evidence which would suggest recent sexual intercourse.

Considering the aforesaid aspects of the matter, I am of the view that without expressing opinion on merits/demerits of the case, petitioner's prayer for grant of regular bail needs to be answered affirmatively.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.
